title: Knowledge Distribution Model
definition: A conceptual model for how knowledge is published, discovered, and verified in a decentralized knowledge ecosystem.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine a library system where books are stored in a central place, but people can use different apps to find and borrow them. This is similar to how CADMIES could function with Glitter and Atlas.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: The knowledge distribution model involves a central storage system (CADMIES DAG), a publishing platform (Glitter), and a discovery platform (Atlas). Scientists publish verified knowledge to the central storage system. Users can discover and use that knowledge through the Glitter or Atlas platforms.
difficulty_levels.expert: The knowledge distribution model is a novel application of distributed systems theory. It combines the rigor of blockchain-based verification (Glitter) with the accessibility of social trust models (Atlas). This model expands on existing decentralized database systems by integrating a central, immutable knowledge layer with multiple publishing and discovery platforms. This allows for a more comprehensive and user-friendly decentralized knowledge ecosystem.

extra_fields.insight: The knowledge distribution model can expand the functionality of a decentralized knowledge ecosystem by integrating multiple publishing and discovery platforms.
